R/00_config.R
content:
# 00_config.R

# Every path, threshold, and setting this pipeline uses lives here.
# Change a value in this file, not wherever it happens to get read.

# CPU cores for the parallel steps (raking per month, building every
# trend table). Not set to all available cores. Each extra core forks
# the whole R session, and this pipeline's data can get wide enough
# that forking across many cores runs slower than running sequentially
# and can exhaust memory. 2 cores measured faster than both sequential
# and a high core count on a real run. Override with the
# PIPELINE_CORES_OVERRIDE env var if you want to try something higher,
# but time it first on a small sample before trusting it on a full run.
PIPELINE_CORES <- as.integer(Sys.getenv("PIPELINE_CORES_OVERRIDE", unset = "2"))

# 1. INPUT FILE PATHS

# These point to files outside this repository: restricted survey data,
# or reference files too large or sensitive to commit. Set the real
# path as an environment variable so it never ends up in git.

# One restricted .sav file per year. {year} is filled in for each year
# in RAPID_CA_MASTERFILE_YEARS. Each yearly file needs the original raw
# columns plus the imputed _imp columns (RaceGroup_imp, region_imp, the
# income and household-size _imp families). Imputation itself runs
# outside this project.
RAPID_CA_MASTERFILE_PATH_TEMPLATE <- Sys.getenv(
  "RAPID_CA_MASTERFILE_PATH_TEMPLATE",
  unset = "PATH_NOT_SET_CA.MasterFile_groupings_{year}.sav"
)
RAPID_CA_MASTERFILE_YEARS <- 2022:2026

# CountyMerged to region mapping (58 CA counties). Lets this pipeline
# re-derive region on its own and check it against the imputation
# team's numbers, instead of only trusting the delivered region_imp
# column. Not respondent-level data, just a small reference table.
COUNTY_REGION_LOOKUP_PATH <- Sys.getenv(
  "COUNTY_REGION_LOOKUP_PATH",
  unset = "PATH_NOT_SET_county_region_lookup.xlsx"
)

# 2. OUTPUT PATHS

# Where the offline pipeline driver writes the small, already
# aggregated tables the dashboard reads.
PIPELINE_OUTPUT_DIR <- "data_pipeline_output"

EXCEL_OUTPUT_DIR <- file.path(PIPELINE_OUTPUT_DIR, "Excel_Tables")

# Internal-only QC material
INTERNAL_QC_OUTPUT_DIR <- "internal_qc_output"

# Respondent-level snapshots of master_core are the same sensitivity as
# the real masterfile, so point this somewhere outside the repo
# entirely if you plan to keep any. Defaults to INTERNAL_QC_OUTPUT_DIR
# (already gitignored) if MASTER_CORE_SNAPSHOT_DIR isn't set. Each run
# still gets its own timestamped subfolder, so re-running never
# overwrites a previous snapshot.
MASTER_CORE_SNAPSHOT_DIR <- Sys.getenv("MASTER_CORE_SNAPSHOT_DIR", unset = INTERNAL_QC_OUTPUT_DIR)

# 3. MINIMUM SAMPLE SIZE (SUPPRESSION) THRESHOLDS

# A month's estimate only shows or exports if it clears these raw
# respondent counts: N_MIN_OVERALL for the CA-wide number,
# N_MIN_SUBGROUP for any one subgroup breakdown.
N_MIN_OVERALL  <- 50
N_MIN_SUBGROUP <- 30

# Source (which survey/panel administration a response came through,
# e.g. "LAEP") is a much finer breakdown than the demographic
# subgroups above -- some sources have far fewer respondents in a
# given month -- so it gets its own, lower bar. 10 is intentionally
# lower than N_MIN_SUBGROUP's 30: tighten this if a specific source
# turns out too thin to say anything reliable even above 10.
N_MIN_SOURCE <- 10

# The rolling average is always the fixed trailing 3 calendar months.
# It never reaches back further to find 3 real months if one is thin
# or missing. Instead a separate, higher threshold applies to the
# cumulative sample size across those exact 3 months. If that sum
# doesn't clear this bar the rolling estimate is suppressed too, even
# if every individual month passed its own 50/30/10 threshold.
ROLLING_MIN_OVERALL  <- 100
ROLLING_MIN_SUBGROUP <- 90
# 3x the monthly Source threshold, matching the ~3x ratio
# ROLLING_MIN_SUBGROUP already uses over N_MIN_SUBGROUP (90 vs 30).
ROLLING_MIN_SOURCE   <- 30

# Month-over-month QC jump checks (R/diagnostics.R:
# compute_month_over_month_jumps()/compute_sample_composition_shifts()),
# run once per pipeline run against that run's own fresh output.
# Percentage POINTS, not a relative/percent change. 10 matches the
# real incident (a ~10pp Food Insecurity jump in both CA Statewide and
# LA County with no obvious cause) that prompted adding this check.
JUMP_CHECK_THRESHOLD_PTS <- 10

# 4. ROLLING AVERAGE WINDOW

# A trailing window: the value shown for month T averages months
# {T, T-1, T-2}.
ROLLING_WINDOW_MONTHS <- 3

# Set to ROLLING_WINDOW_MONTHS instead of 1 if a rolling value should
# only appear once a true 3-month window exists.
ROLLING_MIN_MONTHS_IN_WINDOW <- 1

# Bootstrap replicates behind every rolling margin of error this
# pipeline reports. The same respondent can answer in more than one of
# a rolling window's 3 months, so those rows aren't independent of
# each other. Resampling whole CALIDs instead of rows accounts for
# that correctly, where a plain row-level formula would not. Higher
# n_boot gives a more stable estimate at a roughly linear cost in
# runtime, and this runs once per month/group/outcome row that has a
# real 3-month window, so a wide domain can mean thousands of bootstrap
# calls in one run. 
ROLLING_BOOTSTRAP_N <- 100

# 5. WEIGHTING (RAKING) SETTINGS

# Raking margins are Race, Poverty/income level, and CA Region, fitted
# jointly. No respondent's weight may exceed RAKING_WEIGHT_CAP, so one
# person can't dominate a monthly estimate.
RAKING_WEIGHT_CAP <- 5

# If a month's raking fails to converge, or has too few eligible
# respondents, it pools with prior months (up to a 3-month window)
# before giving up.
RAKING_MIN_N_BEFORE_POOLING <- 50

# The weight column name added to master_core. Update here if the
# scheme ever changes.
RAKE_WEIGHT_COL <- "rake_weight_rpr_cap5"

# California ACS population targets raking corrects toward, for each
# of the 3 margins.If a new ACS vintage comes out, recompute the marginals and
# paste the updated numbers in below.
ACS_TARGETS_RPR <- list(
  race_group_5cat = c(
    White                                   = 0.299971,
    Black                                   = 0.050653,
    Latinx                                  = 0.447785,
    `Asian/Native Hawaiian/Pacific Islander` = 0.153688,
    `Other racial and ethnic groups`        = 0.047902
  ),
  poverty_cat = c(
    `At or Below 100% FPL` = 0.124327,
    `101-200% FPL`         = 0.184157,
    `201-400% FPL`         = 0.285396,
    `Above 400% FPL`       = 0.406120
  ),
  ca_region = c(
    `Urban North` = 0.265641,
    `Urban South` = 0.557428,
    Suburban      = 0.159728,
    Rural         = 0.017203
  )
)

# 6. GROUPING VARIABLES

# The confirmed demographic breakdowns this pipeline reports.
# Race, CA Region, and Income Level come from imputed-and-LOCF'd columns. 
# The other three have no imputed tier and come from LOCF-only columns.
GROUPING_VARS <- list(
  "Race"                             = "race_group_4cat",
  "Income Level"                     = "poverty_cat",
  "CA Region"                        = "ca_region",
  "Household Child Age"              = "hh_child_age_mix",
  "Child Disability"                 = "disability_locf",
  "Dual/Non-Dual Parent Household"   = "single_parent_locf"
)

# Display order for a sample-description table's Category column.
# Overall first, then each grouping above, then Source last.
DEFAULT_SAMPLE_DESCRIPTION_CATEGORY_ORDER <- c("Overall", names(GROUPING_VARS), "Source")

# The 4 possible values of poverty_cat. Kept here, not in 01_prep.R, so
# the dashboard and report can use this order without sourcing prep
# logic they don't need.
POVERTY_CAT_LEVELS <- c(
  "At or Below 100% FPL", "101-200% FPL", "201-400% FPL", "Above 400% FPL"
)

# The 2 possible values of poverty_200_cat. Exactly 200% FPL falls in
# the lower group, matching the 4-level convention above.
POVERTY_200_CAT_LEVELS <- c("At or Below 200% FPL", "Above 200% FPL")

# Display order for grouping levels that aren't naturally alphabetical.
# Income Level's FPL bands sort wrong alphabetically (the lowest band
# ends up last), so its order is spelled out here. Any grouping not
# listed falls back to a plain alphabetical sort.
GROUPING_LEVEL_ORDER <- list(
  "Income Level" = POVERTY_CAT_LEVELS
)

#' Order a grouping's level values for display.
#' @param levels_present The distinct level values actually present.
#' @param grouping_label Which grouping these levels belong to.
#' @return levels_present in GROUPING_LEVEL_ORDER's order if one is
#'   defined, otherwise a plain alphabetical sort.
order_grouping_levels <- function(levels_present, grouping_label) {
  canonical <- GROUPING_LEVEL_ORDER[[grouping_label]]
  if (is.null(canonical)) return(sort(levels_present))
  canonical[canonical %in% levels_present]
}

# 7. RAPID-CA BRANDING CONSTANTS
RAPID_COLORS <- list(
  yellow      = "#FEE11A",  # primary brand color, single-series charts and accents
  light_fog   = "#F4F4F4",
  white       = "#FFFFFF",
  gray        = "#464646",
  soft_black  = "#2E2D29",  # primary text color on light/yellow backgrounds
  warm_red    = "#F4795B",  # secondary, use sparingly
  purple      = "#D7AEFF",  # secondary
  sky_blue    = "#67AFD2"   # secondary
)

RAPID_FONT_FAMILY <- "Manrope"

# 8. SHARED TREND-PLOT COLOR SYSTEM
# Used by both the static report figures and the interactive dashboard

TREND_SERIES_COLORS <- c(Monthly = RAPID_COLORS$soft_black, Rolling = RAPID_COLORS$soft_black)

LEVEL_COLOR_PALETTE <- c(
  RAPID_COLORS$sky_blue, RAPID_COLORS$warm_red,
  RAPID_COLORS$purple, RAPID_COLORS$gray, "#2E7D32", "#8D6E63", "#5C6BC0"
)

# Specific level labels that always get the same color, regardless of
# where alphabetical order would otherwise put them. Each pair/trio
# below is checked for color-vision-deficiency safety before use.
FIXED_LEVEL_COLORS <- c(
  # Parent Distress's two thresholds: higher severity always near-black,
  # lower always mid-gray.
  "Very frequent"              = "#1A1A1A",
  "At least somewhat frequent" = "#999999",
  # Child Behavior's own wording, same color pair.
  "Often or very true"      = "#1A1A1A",
  "At least sometimes true" = "#999999",
  # Food Insecurity's 3 severity levels. "Overall" uses the same mid-gray
  # already validated above for Parent Distress/Child Behavior's lower threshold
  "Overall"  = "#999999",
  "Moderate" = "#808080",
  "Severe"   = "#262626",
  # Child Care's 3 types: grayscale on purpose, light to dark.
  "Parent-Only Care"      = "#CFCFCF",
  "Center-Based Care"     = "#808080",
  "Non-Center-Based Care" = "#262626",
  # Material Hardship's sources.
  "Food"       = RAPID_COLORS$warm_red,
  "Housing"    = RAPID_COLORS$purple,
  "Utility"    = RAPID_COLORS$sky_blue,
  "Healthcare" = "#2E7D32"
)

#' @param levels Character vector of level names to color.
#' @return A named vector, level to hex color. A level with a
#'   FIXED_LEVEL_COLORS entry always gets that color. Every other level
#'   cycles through LEVEL_COLOR_PALETTE by its sorted position among
#'   the remaining levels.
build_level_color_map <- function(levels) {
  sorted_levels <- sort(unique(levels))
  fixed <- FIXED_LEVEL_COLORS[sorted_levels]
  is_fixed <- !is.na(fixed)

  remaining <- sorted_levels[!is_fixed]
  if (length(remaining) > 0) {
    # Skip any palette color already claimed by a fixed level in this
    # set, so a fallback level can't land on the same color as one that
    # was pinned on purpose.
    available_palette <- setdiff(LEVEL_COLOR_PALETTE, unname(fixed[is_fixed]))
    if (length(available_palette) == 0) available_palette <- LEVEL_COLOR_PALETTE
    fixed[!is_fixed] <- available_palette[((seq_along(remaining) - 1) %% length(available_palette)) + 1]
  }
  stats::setNames(unname(fixed), sorted_levels)
}

# 9. THE INVESTIGATE VIEW'S PER-GROUPING COLORS
# A different rule from LEVEL_COLOR_PALETTE above. That one colors a
# chart's lines by level. The Investigate tab's deviation-bar chart
# shows several groupings at once side by side, so color there answers
# "which grouping does this bar belong to," one fixed color per
# grouping.
GROUPING_COLORS <- c(
  "Race"                             = RAPID_COLORS$sky_blue,
  "Income Level"                     = RAPID_COLORS$warm_red,
  "CA Region"                        = RAPID_COLORS$purple,
  "Household Child Age"              = "#2E7D32",
  "Child Disability"                 = "#8D6E63",
  "Dual/Non-Dual Parent Household"   = "#5C6BC0",
  "LA County"                        = RAPID_COLORS$gray
)

content:
# 04_summarize.R
# Turns respondent-level rows into monthly and 3-month-rolling summary
# tables, with both a weighted and an unweighted percentage.
#
# calc_prop_summary() makes one row per month (or month x group) with
# the weighted/unweighted proportion, margin of error, n, and a
# suppressed/suppress_reason pair. calc_rolling_avg() takes that output
# and adds the 3-month trailing rolling version as new columns.
#
# compute_trend_averages() / format_trend_subtitle() give two summary
# numbers: an n-weighted average (bigger months count more) and a plain
# unweighted average (every month counts equally).

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Precision helpers (MOE, effective sample size)

# Margin of error for a weighted proportion, using the design-effect
# based effective sample size. A month that needed heavy reweighting to
# hit the ACS targets gets a wider MOE here even if its raw n looks fine.
weighted_moe_prop <- function(binary_values, weights, alpha = 0.05) {
  ok <- !is.na(binary_values) & !is.na(weights)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  x <- binary_values[ok]
  w <- weights[ok]

  p     <- stats::weighted.mean(x, w)
  n_eff <- effective_n(w)
  se    <- sqrt(p * (1 - p) / n_eff)
  stats::qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * se
}

# Standard margin of error for an unweighted proportion.
unweighted_moe_prop <- function(prop, n, alpha = 0.05) {
  if (is.na(prop) || is.na(n) || n == 0) return(NA_real_)
  stats::qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * sqrt(prop * (1 - prop) / n)
}

# Effective sample size from raking weights. Equals the raw n when every
# weight is equal, shrinks as weights become more unequal.
effective_n <- function(weights) {
  w <- weights[!is.na(weights)]
  if (length(w) == 0) return(NA_real_)
  sum(w)^2 / sum(w^2)
}

# Weighted mean that returns NA if nothing's valid to average, dropping
# a row if either the outcome or the weight is missing for it.
safe_weighted_mean <- function(x, w) {
  ok <- !is.na(x) & !is.na(w)
  if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
  stats::weighted.mean(x[ok], w[ok])
}

# 2. Monthly summary (weighted and unweighted)

# One row per month (or month x group) with the weighted and unweighted
# percentage for one 0/1 outcome column, plus everything needed to plot
# a confidence band and suppress unreliable months.
#
# @param df Respondent-level data with month, outcome_var, weight_var.
# @param outcome_var Name of the 0/1 outcome column.
# @param group_var Optional grouping column. NULL means overall.
# @param weight_var Name of the raking weight column.
# @param min_n Minimum respondents for a row to count as shown rather
#   than suppressed.
# @param id_col Respondent ID column, used to add n_participants
#   (distinct respondents that month) alongside n (response count). They
#   only differ if someone answers more than once in a single month.
# @return One row per month (x group) that exists in the data at all. A
#   month is never dropped here, even at zero or very low n.
#   suppressed is TRUE if the row shouldn't be shown. suppress_reason
#   distinguishes zero valid responses from below-minimum from included.
calc_prop_summary <- function(df, outcome_var, group_var = NULL,
                               weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL,
                               month_var = "month",
                               id_col = "CALID",
                               min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) N_MIN_OVERALL else N_MIN_SUBGROUP) {
  group_cols <- c(month_var, group_var)

  # Every (month [x group]) combination
  all_combos <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[month_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::distinct(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(group_cols)))

  answered_stats <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_var]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(group_cols))) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      n               = dplyr::n(),
      n_participants  = dplyr::n_distinct(.data[[id_col]]),
      n_eff           = effective_n(.data[[weight_var]]),
      unweighted_prop = mean(.data[[outcome_var]]),
      unweighted_moe  = unweighted_moe_prop(mean(.data[[outcome_var]]), dplyr::n()),
      weighted_prop   = safe_weighted_mean(.data[[outcome_var]], .data[[weight_var]]),
      weighted_moe    = weighted_moe_prop(.data[[outcome_var]], .data[[weight_var]]),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  all_combos %>%
    dplyr::left_join(answered_stats, by = group_cols) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      n = tidyr::replace_na(n, 0L),
      n_participants = tidyr::replace_na(n_participants, 0L),
      unweighted_ci_low  = pmax(0, unweighted_prop - unweighted_moe),
      unweighted_ci_high = pmin(1, unweighted_prop + unweighted_moe),
      weighted_ci_low    = pmax(0, weighted_prop - weighted_moe),
      weighted_ci_high   = pmin(1, weighted_prop + weighted_moe),
      date = as.Date(paste0(gsub("/", "-", .data[[month_var]]), "-01")),
      suppressed = n < min_n,
      suppress_reason = dplyr::case_when(
        n == 0    ~ "No valid responses this month (item may not have been fielded, or nobody answered it)",
        n < min_n ~ sprintf("Suppressed: n = %d is below the required minimum of %d", n, min_n),
        TRUE      ~ "Included"
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(date)
}

# Runs calc_prop_summary() over several outcome columns at once, e.g.
# the 4 Parent Distress measures, stacking the results long with an
# "outcome" label column.
# @param outcome_vars A named character vector, names are display
#   labels, values are column names.
calc_multi_prop_summary <- function(df, outcome_vars, group_var = NULL,
                                     weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL,
                                     month_var = "month",
                                     min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) N_MIN_OVERALL else N_MIN_SUBGROUP) {
  purrr::imap_dfr(outcome_vars, function(col, label) {
    calc_prop_summary(df, outcome_var = col, group_var = group_var,
                       weight_var = weight_var, month_var = month_var,
                       min_n = min_n) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(outcome = label)
  })
}

# 3. Rolling average (3-month trailing)
# Adds the 3-month trailing rolling average (month T uses T, T-1, T-2)
# as new columns. This is a post-processing smoothing step: the rolling
# weighted % is a mean of the last window months' already-computed
# weighted_prop values, not a fresh weighted.mean() over pooled rows.

# @param monthly_data Output of calc_prop_summary() (or
#   calc_multi_prop_summary() with group_var = "outcome", so each
#   outcome rolls independently). Pass the unfiltered table (every
#   month, suppressed or not); a month suppressed on its own can still
#   contribute toward a reliable 3-month total.
# @param group_var Optional column to roll independently within (a
#   subgroup, or "outcome" for multi-measure data). NULL rolls the whole
#   table as one series.
# @param window Months in the trailing window.
# @param min_months_in_window Minimum months required before a row gets
#   a rolling value at all.
# @param min_n Minimum cumulative n across the window for a row to
#   count as shown rather than suppressed. Deliberately higher than the
#   monthly threshold, since this certifies 3 pooled months, not 1.
# @param raw_df Respondent-level rows, scoped the same way monthly_data
#   was built. When given, the rolling margin of error is computed by
#   resampling whole CALIDs (cluster_bootstrap_rolling_se()), which
#   correctly accounts for the same person showing up in more than one
#   of a window's 3 months. When NULL, falls back to a plain average of
#   the window's monthly MOEs, so this function still works without
#   underlying rows available.
# @param outcome_var The raw outcome column name, when every series
#   rolls the same outcome. Ignored if outcome_var_lookup is given.
# @param outcome_var_lookup Named vector, label to raw column name, for
#   when monthly_data has an "outcome" column covering several outcome
#   variables in one call.
# @param demographic_group_var The real raw-data column name to filter
#   raw_df by subgroup level. Not necessarily the same as this
#   function's own group_var, which can just be a series key. NULL
#   means no subgroup filtering.
# @param weight_var,id_col,date_col,n_boot Passed through to
#   cluster_bootstrap_rolling_se().
# @return monthly_data with rolling_* columns added, including
#   window_months (the exact 3 calendar months this row's window
#   covers, always the fixed trailing span), rolling_suppressed, and
#   rolling_suppress_reason.
calc_rolling_avg <- function(monthly_data, group_var = NULL,
                              window = ROLLING_WINDOW_MONTHS,
                              min_months_in_window = ROLLING_MIN_MONTHS_IN_WINDOW,
                              min_n = ROLLING_MIN_OVERALL,
                              raw_df = NULL, outcome_var = NULL, outcome_var_lookup = NULL,
                              demographic_group_var = NULL, weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL,
                              id_col = "CALID", date_col = "StartDate",
                              n_boot = ROLLING_BOOTSTRAP_N) {

  compute_rolling_one_series <- function(one_series) {
    one_series <- one_series %>% dplyr::arrange(date)
    n_rows <- nrow(one_series)

    # This series' own raw outcome column and its matching subgroup
    # slice of raw_df, resolved once per series rather than per row,
    # since neither changes across the series' own rows.
    series_outcome_col <- NULL
    series_raw_df <- NULL
    if (!is.null(raw_df)) {
      series_outcome_col <- if (!is.null(outcome_var)) {
        outcome_var
      } else if (!is.null(outcome_var_lookup) && "outcome" %in% names(one_series)) {
        outcome_var_lookup[[one_series$outcome[1]]]
      } else {
        NULL
      }
      if (!is.null(series_outcome_col)) {
        series_raw_df <- raw_df
        if (!is.null(demographic_group_var) && demographic_group_var %in% names(one_series) &&
            demographic_group_var %in% names(raw_df)) {
          lvl <- one_series[[demographic_group_var]][1]
          series_raw_df <- series_raw_df[series_raw_df[[demographic_group_var]] == lvl, ]
        }
      }
    }
    use_bootstrap <- !is.null(series_raw_df) && !is.null(series_outcome_col)

    window_months           <- rep(NA_character_, n_rows)
    n_months_in_window      <- rep(0L, n_rows)
    rolling_n               <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
    rolling_weighted_prop   <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
    rolling_weighted_moe    <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
    rolling_unweighted_prop <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)
    rolling_unweighted_moe  <- rep(NA_real_, n_rows)

    for (i in seq_len(n_rows)) {
      # The fixed trailing span: this row's calendar month and the
      # window - 1 months immediately before it. Always exactly these
      # dates, whether or not a row exists for all of them.
      window_dates <- seq(one_series$date[i], by = "-1 month", length.out = window)
      idx <- match(window_dates, one_series$date)  # NA for any date with no row at all (a true gap)

      window_months[i]      <- paste(format(sort(window_dates), "%Y/%m"), collapse = ", ")
      n_months_in_window[i] <- sum(!is.na(idx) & !is.na(one_series$weighted_prop[idx]))

      if (n_months_in_window[i] < min_months_in_window) next

      rolling_n[i]               <- sum(one_series$n[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
      rolling_weighted_prop[i]   <- mean(one_series$weighted_prop[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
      rolling_unweighted_prop[i] <- mean(one_series$unweighted_prop[idx], na.rm = TRUE)

      if (use_bootstrap) {
        boot <- cluster_bootstrap_rolling_se(
          series_raw_df, series_outcome_col, weight_var = weight_var,
          id_col = id_col, date_col = date_col,
          window_dates = window_dates, n_boot = n_boot
        )
        rolling_weighted_moe[i]   <- boot$boot_moe
        rolling_unweighted_moe[i] <- boot$unweighted_boot_moe
      } else {
        # No raw_df given, so fall back to a plain average of the
        # window's own per-month MOEs.
        rolling_weighted_moe[i]   <- mean(one_series$weighted_moe[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
        rolling_unweighted_moe[i] <- mean(one_series$unweighted_moe[idx], na.rm = TRUE)
      }
    }

    one_series %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        n_months_in_window     = n_months_in_window,
        window_months           = window_months,
        rolling_n               = rolling_n,
        rolling_weighted_prop   = rolling_weighted_prop,
        rolling_weighted_moe    = rolling_weighted_moe,
        rolling_unweighted_prop = rolling_unweighted_prop,
        rolling_unweighted_moe  = rolling_unweighted_moe,
        rolling_weighted_ci_low    = pmax(0, rolling_weighted_prop - rolling_weighted_moe),
        rolling_weighted_ci_high   = pmin(1, rolling_weighted_prop + rolling_weighted_moe),
        rolling_unweighted_ci_low  = pmax(0, rolling_unweighted_prop - rolling_unweighted_moe),
        rolling_unweighted_ci_high = pmin(1, rolling_unweighted_prop + rolling_unweighted_moe),
        rolling_suppressed = is.na(rolling_n) | rolling_n < min_n,
        rolling_suppress_reason = dplyr::case_when(
          is.na(rolling_n) ~ "No rolling average yet (no real month in the trailing 3-month window)",
          rolling_n < min_n ~ sprintf(
            "Suppressed: 3-month cumulative n = %d is below the required minimum of %d", rolling_n, min_n
          ),
          TRUE ~ "Included"
        )
      )
  }

  if (!is.null(group_var) && group_var %in% names(monthly_data)) {
    monthly_data %>%
      dplyr::group_by(.data[[group_var]]) %>%
      dplyr::group_modify(~ compute_rolling_one_series(.x)) %>%
      dplyr::ungroup()
  } else {
    compute_rolling_one_series(monthly_data)
  }
}

# 3b. CALID-clustered bootstrap for the 3-month rolling average
#
# The same CALID can appear in more than one of a rolling window's 3
# months, anyone retained in the panel across waves. Those repeated
# responses aren't independent of each other, so a plain average of
# each month's own margin of error treats them as if they were, which
# can misstate the real uncertainty of the rolling estimate. This
# resamples whole CALIDs instead of rows, so a person who appears in 2
# of the 3 months is resampled, or not, as a single unit, keeping
# whatever correlation their repeated answers carry.
#
# rolling_prop_from_rows() reproduces the same point estimate
# calc_rolling_avg() computes from raw rows (the mean of each month's
# own weighted proportion, not one proportion pooled across all rows at
# once), so the bootstrap's SE is a correct replacement for the old
# margin of error, for the same estimator.

#' @param df Respondent-level rows, not yet filtered to the window,
#'   this filters internally so you can pass data already filtered to
#'   whatever single grouping level you care about.
#' @param window_dates The exact 3 calendar month-start Dates this
#'   window covers (e.g. from calc_rolling_avg()'s own
#'   `window_dates <- seq(date[i], by = "-1 month", length.out = window)`).
#' @param weighted TRUE reproduces rolling_weighted_prop (mean of each
#'   month's weighted proportion). FALSE reproduces
#'   rolling_unweighted_prop (mean of each month's plain unweighted
#'   proportion); weight_var is ignored in that case.
#' @return The rolling prop value computed directly from rows, or NA if
#'   no month in the window has any valid (CALID, outcome[, weight]) row.
rolling_prop_from_rows <- function(df, outcome_var, weight_var, date_col, window_dates, weighted = TRUE) {
  month_date <- floor_to_month_date(df[[date_col]])
  monthly_props <- vapply(window_dates, function(d) {
    if (weighted) {
      in_month <- month_date == d & !is.na(df[[outcome_var]]) & !is.na(df[[weight_var]])
      if (!any(in_month, na.rm = TRUE)) return(NA_real_)
      safe_weighted_mean(df[[outcome_var]][in_month], df[[weight_var]][in_month])
    } else {
      in_month <- month_date == d & !is.na(df[[outcome_var]])
      if (!any(in_month, na.rm = TRUE)) return(NA_real_)
      mean(df[[outcome_var]][in_month])
    }
  }, numeric(1))
  if (all(is.na(monthly_props))) return(NA_real_)
  mean(monthly_props, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Snaps a date down to the 1st of its own month. Respondent-level
# StartDate is an actual survey date, not already floored the way the
# monthly summary table's date column is.
floor_to_month_date <- function(dates) {
  as.Date(format(as.Date(dates), "%Y-%m-01"))
}

#' CALID-clustered bootstrap SE/MOE for one rolling 3-month window, one
#' outcome, already filtered to one grouping level.
#'
#' @param df Respondent-level rows for this one grouping level, not yet
#'   filtered to the window or to non-missing outcome rows, that
#'   happens internally.
#' @param outcome_var,weight_var,id_col,date_col Column names.
#' @param window_dates The exact 3 calendar month-start dates this
#'   window covers.
#' @param n_boot Number of bootstrap replicates. Higher gives a more
#'   stable SE at a roughly linear cost in runtime.
#' @param alpha For the normal-approximation MOE.
#' @return A list with both the weighted and unweighted bootstrap
#'   results for this window, computed from the same resampled
#'   replicates each iteration: point_estimate, boot_se, boot_moe,
#'   boot_ci_low, boot_ci_high, naive_moe, and the unweighted_ versions
#'   of each, plus n_boot and n_clusters. naive_moe is the plain,
#'   clustering-blind margin of error for the same data, included so
#'   boot_moe can be compared against it directly. The boot_* fields are
#'   NA if fewer than 2 CALIDs are in the window.
cluster_bootstrap_rolling_se <- function(df, outcome_var, weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL,
                                          id_col = "CALID", date_col = "StartDate",
                                          window_dates, n_boot = ROLLING_BOOTSTRAP_N, alpha = 0.05) {
  # Everything below works on plain vectors, not a data frame, since
  # this runs once per month/group/outcome row across the pipeline,
  # each time looping n_boot replicates. month_idx (an integer index
  # into window_dates) replaces a date comparison per replicate with a
  # plain integer comparison, computed once up front.
  month_date <- floor_to_month_date(df[[date_col]])
  keep <- month_date %in% window_dates & !is.na(df[[outcome_var]])
  outcome     <- df[[outcome_var]][keep]
  real_weight <- df[[weight_var]][keep]
  calid_chr   <- as.character(df[[id_col]])[keep]
  month_idx   <- match(month_date[keep], window_dates)
  n_window    <- length(window_dates)

  # The point estimate is called once per window, not per replicate, so
  # it goes through rolling_prop_from_rows() directly, keeping exactly
  # one implementation of this estimator.
  point_estimate            <- rolling_prop_from_rows(df, outcome_var, weight_var, date_col, window_dates, weighted = TRUE)
  unweighted_point_estimate <- rolling_prop_from_rows(df, outcome_var, weight_var, date_col, window_dates, weighted = FALSE)

  # rolling_stat() below is a fast, vector-based version of the same
  # estimator, used only inside the replicate loop further down, where
  # rolling_prop_from_rows()'s per-call date parsing made the bootstrap
  # too slow at real pipeline scale. w = NULL means an unweighted calc.
  # Otherwise w is whatever weight the caller supplies: a replicate
  # weight (how many times a row's CALID was drawn) for a resample,
  # including the unweighted resample, where w = rep_weight alone is
  # what makes a CALID drawn twice count twice. o/idx/w must always be
  # the same length, aligned by position, so a resampled row's outcome
  # lines up with its own month and weight.
  rolling_stat <- function(o, idx, w) {
    monthly <- vapply(seq_len(n_window), function(m) {
      in_month <- idx == m & (if (is.null(w)) TRUE else !is.na(w))
      if (!any(in_month)) return(NA_real_)
      if (is.null(w)) mean(o[in_month]) else stats::weighted.mean(o[in_month], w[in_month])
    }, numeric(1))
    if (all(is.na(monthly))) return(NA_real_)
    mean(monthly, na.rm = TRUE)
  }

  monthly_moes <- vapply(seq_len(n_window), function(m) {
    in_month <- month_idx == m & !is.na(real_weight)
    if (!any(in_month)) return(NA_real_)
    weighted_moe_prop(outcome[in_month], real_weight[in_month], alpha = alpha)
  }, numeric(1))
  naive_moe <- mean(monthly_moes, na.rm = TRUE)

  unweighted_monthly_moes <- vapply(seq_len(n_window), function(m) {
    in_month <- month_idx == m
    if (!any(in_month)) return(NA_real_)
    unweighted_moe_prop(mean(outcome[in_month]), sum(in_month), alpha = alpha)
  }, numeric(1))
  unweighted_naive_moe <- mean(unweighted_monthly_moes, na.rm = TRUE)

  clusters <- unique(calid_chr)
  n_clusters <- length(clusters)

  empty_result <- function() {
    list(point_estimate = point_estimate, boot_se = NA_real_, boot_moe = NA_real_,
         boot_ci_low = NA_real_, boot_ci_high = NA_real_, naive_moe = naive_moe,
         unweighted_point_estimate = unweighted_point_estimate,
         unweighted_boot_se = NA_real_, unweighted_boot_moe = NA_real_,
         unweighted_boot_ci_low = NA_real_, unweighted_boot_ci_high = NA_real_,
         unweighted_naive_moe = unweighted_naive_moe,
         n_boot = 0L, n_clusters = n_clusters)
  }
  if (n_clusters < 2) return(empty_result())

  # Pre-split row indices by CALID once, avoiding re-filtering on every
  # replicate.
  rows_by_calid <- split(seq_along(calid_chr), calid_chr)

  weighted_stats   <- vector("numeric", n_boot)
  unweighted_stats <- vector("numeric", n_boot)
  for (b in seq_len(n_boot)) {
    sampled_calids <- sample(clusters, size = n_clusters, replace = TRUE)
    # How many times each CALID was drawn this replicate, applied as a
    # multiplicative weight instead of literally duplicating rows.
    draw_counts <- table(sampled_calids)
    row_idx  <- unlist(rows_by_calid[names(draw_counts)], use.names = FALSE)
    rep_w    <- as.numeric(draw_counts)[match(calid_chr[row_idx], names(draw_counts))]

    weighted_stats[b]   <- rolling_stat(outcome[row_idx], month_idx[row_idx], real_weight[row_idx] * rep_w)
    unweighted_stats[b] <- rolling_stat(outcome[row_idx], month_idx[row_idx], rep_w)
  }
  weighted_stats   <- weighted_stats[!is.na(weighted_stats)]
  unweighted_stats <- unweighted_stats[!is.na(unweighted_stats)]

  boot_se  <- if (length(weighted_stats) >= 2) stats::sd(weighted_stats) else NA_real_
  boot_moe <- if (is.na(boot_se)) NA_real_ else stats::qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * boot_se

  unweighted_boot_se  <- if (length(unweighted_stats) >= 2) stats::sd(unweighted_stats) else NA_real_
  unweighted_boot_moe <- if (is.na(unweighted_boot_se)) NA_real_ else stats::qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * unweighted_boot_se

  list(
    point_estimate = point_estimate,
    boot_se        = boot_se,
    boot_moe       = boot_moe,
    boot_ci_low    = if (is.na(boot_moe)) NA_real_ else pmax(0, point_estimate - boot_moe),
    boot_ci_high   = if (is.na(boot_moe)) NA_real_ else pmin(1, point_estimate + boot_moe),
    naive_moe      = naive_moe,
    unweighted_point_estimate = unweighted_point_estimate,
    unweighted_boot_se        = unweighted_boot_se,
    unweighted_boot_moe       = unweighted_boot_moe,
    unweighted_boot_ci_low    = if (is.na(unweighted_boot_moe)) NA_real_ else pmax(0, unweighted_point_estimate - unweighted_boot_moe),
    unweighted_boot_ci_high   = if (is.na(unweighted_boot_moe)) NA_real_ else pmin(1, unweighted_point_estimate + unweighted_boot_moe),
    unweighted_naive_moe      = unweighted_naive_moe,
    n_boot         = length(weighted_stats),
    n_clusters     = n_clusters
  )
}

# 4. Sample-size totals (post-suppression)

# Total number of responses and total number of unique participants
# (distinct CALIDs) behind a trend.
# @param df The full respondent-level data calc_prop_summary() ran on.
# @param outcome_var Name of the 0/1 outcome column.
# @param monthly_data calc_prop_summary()'s output for this same
#   outcome_var/group_var.
# @param group_var Optional grouping column, returns one row per level
#   instead of one overall row.
# @return A tibble, one row overall or one row per group level, each
#   with total_responses and total_participants.
compute_trend_totals <- function(df, outcome_var, monthly_data, group_var = NULL,
                                  id_col = "CALID", month_var = "month") {
  answered <- df %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome_var]]))
  surviving <- dplyr::filter(monthly_data, !suppressed)

  count_totals <- function(data) {
    tibble::tibble(
      total_responses    = nrow(data),
      total_participants = dplyr::n_distinct(data[[id_col]])
    )
  }

  if (is.null(group_var)) {
    kept <- answered %>% dplyr::filter(.data[[month_var]] %in% surviving[[month_var]])
    count_totals(kept)
  } else {
    purrr::map_dfr(sort(unique(stats::na.omit(surviving[[group_var]]))), function(lvl) {
      lvl_months <- surviving[[month_var]][surviving[[group_var]] == lvl]
      kept <- answered %>%
        dplyr::filter(.data[[group_var]] == lvl, .data[[month_var]] %in% lvl_months)
      dplyr::bind_cols(stats::setNames(list(lvl), group_var), count_totals(kept))
    })
  }
}

# 5. Subtitle summary numbers: n-weighted average and unweighted average
# Computed from the monthly (not rolling) weighted %:
#   n_weighted_avg : the n-weighted average of each month's weighted %,
#                     bigger months count more.
#   unweighted_avg : plain mean of the monthly weighted % values, every
#                     month counts equally.

# @param monthly_data Output of calc_prop_summary(), already filtered
#   to non-suppressed rows.
# @param prop_col Which column to average.
compute_trend_averages <- function(monthly_data, prop_col = "weighted_prop", n_col = "n") {
  props <- monthly_data[[prop_col]]
  ns    <- monthly_data[[n_col]]
  ok    <- !is.na(props) & !is.na(ns)

  list(
    n_weighted_avg = sum(props[ok] * ns[ok]) / sum(ns[ok]),
    unweighted_avg = mean(props[ok])
  )
}

# Formats compute_trend_averages() (and optionally compute_trend_totals())
# as the subtitle string every plot uses.
# @param totals Optional single-row output of compute_trend_totals(),
#   if given, adds a second line reporting how much data the trend is
#   based on.
format_trend_subtitle <- function(monthly_data, prop_col = "weighted_prop", n_col = "n", totals = NULL) {
  avgs <- compute_trend_averages(monthly_data, prop_col, n_col)
  base <- sprintf(
    "N-weighted average: %.1f%%  |  Unweighted average: %.1f%%",
    avgs$n_weighted_avg * 100, avgs$unweighted_avg * 100
  )
  if (is.null(totals)) return(base)

  paste0(
    base, "\n",
    sprintf(
      "Based on %s responses from %s unique participants (months below the minimum sample size excluded)",
      format(totals$total_responses, big.mark = ","), format(totals$total_participants, big.mark = ",")
    )
  )
}

# 6. Convenience wrappers: monthly + rolling + totals together, in one call

# Monthly + rolling + totals together, for one outcome.
# @param min_n Monthly suppression threshold.
# @param rolling_min_n Cumulative 3-month suppression threshold,
#   independent of min_n since a month can be individually too thin to
#   show on its own yet still contribute to a reliable pooled estimate.
# @return list(monthly, rolling: only the surviving rows, what plots
#   use; monthly_all, rolling_all: every row including suppressed ones,
#   with why; totals: total_responses/total_participants from the
#   surviving months).
calc_trend <- function(df, outcome_var, group_var = NULL,
                        weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL, month_var = "month",
                        min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) N_MIN_OVERALL else N_MIN_SUBGROUP,
                        rolling_min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) ROLLING_MIN_OVERALL else ROLLING_MIN_SUBGROUP) {
  monthly_all <- calc_prop_summary(df, outcome_var, group_var = group_var,
                                    weight_var = weight_var, month_var = month_var, min_n = min_n)
  monthly <- dplyr::filter(monthly_all, !suppressed)
  rolling_all <- calc_rolling_avg(monthly_all, group_var = group_var, min_n = rolling_min_n,
                                   raw_df = df, outcome_var = outcome_var,
                                   demographic_group_var = group_var, weight_var = weight_var)
  rolling <- dplyr::filter(rolling_all, !rolling_suppressed)
  totals  <- compute_trend_totals(df, outcome_var, monthly_all, group_var = group_var, month_var = month_var)

  list(monthly = monthly, rolling = rolling, monthly_all = monthly_all, rolling_all = rolling_all, totals = totals)
}

# Monthly + rolling + totals together, for several outcomes at once,
# e.g. the 4 Parent Distress measures. totals has one row per outcome,
# since each measure can have different missingness and suppression.
calc_multi_trend <- function(df, outcome_vars, group_var = NULL,
                              weight_var = RAKE_WEIGHT_COL, month_var = "month",
                              min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) N_MIN_OVERALL else N_MIN_SUBGROUP,
                              rolling_min_n = if (is.null(group_var)) ROLLING_MIN_OVERALL else ROLLING_MIN_SUBGROUP) {
  monthly_all <- calc_multi_prop_summary(df, outcome_vars, group_var = group_var,
                                          weight_var = weight_var, month_var = month_var, min_n = min_n)
  monthly <- dplyr::filter(monthly_all, !suppressed)

  if (is.null(group_var)) {
    # Only "outcome" distinguishes one series from another.
    rolling_all <- calc_rolling_avg(monthly_all, group_var = "outcome", min_n = rolling_min_n,
                                     raw_df = df, outcome_var_lookup = outcome_vars, weight_var = weight_var)
  } else {
    rolling_all <- monthly_all %>%
      dplyr::mutate(.trend_key = paste(outcome, .data[[group_var]])) %>%
      calc_rolling_avg(group_var = ".trend_key", min_n = rolling_min_n,
                        raw_df = df, outcome_var_lookup = outcome_vars,
                        demographic_group_var = group_var, weight_var = weight_var) %>%
      dplyr::select(-.trend_key)
  }
  rolling <- dplyr::filter(rolling_all, !rolling_suppressed)

  totals <- purrr::imap_dfr(outcome_vars, function(col, label) {
    compute_trend_totals(df, col, dplyr::filter(monthly_all, outcome == label),
                          group_var = group_var, month_var = month_var) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(outcome = label, .before = 1)
  })

  list(monthly = monthly, rolling = rolling, monthly_all = monthly_all, rolling_all = rolling_all, totals = totals)
}

# 05_excel_export.R

# Exports every domain's weighted monthly and 3-month-rolling estimates
# to Excel workbooks. One workbook per domain, one tab per grouping cut
# (Overall, then each demographic grouping, then LA County). A styled
# header block per group level, stacked vertically in a tab, or (for
# multi-measure domains) one header block per outcome with the group
# blocks nested inside that.
#
# Each table has Month, N, Monthly %, Rolling N, 3-Month Rolling %.
# Weighted only. Unweighted numbers live in the plots and the
# dashboard's download table instead. Excel also gets 3 extra columns
# the plots don't show: Rolling Window (the 3 calendar months a Rolling
# % was averaged from), Reason (why a month's Monthly % is suppressed),
# and Rolling Reason (same idea for the Rolling %, tracked separately
# since a thin month can still contribute to a reliable 3-month total).
#
# export_all_domains() takes the SAME cuts R/06_reporting.R already
# computed for the dashboard's trend tables, rather than recomputing
# calc_trend()/calc_multi_trend() a second time. The rolling margin of
# error now runs a real bootstrap, so computing it twice for the same
# numbers is expensive for nothing.


library(openxlsx)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)



# 1. Which columns make up each domain's outcome(s)

# Single-outcome domains export one sheet set. Multi-outcome domains get
# one outcome header block per measure inside each grouping tab. Names
# are the display labels used in the outcome header; values are the 0/1
# column names.

MATERIAL_HARDSHIP_TYPES <- c(
  Food        = "fs_food",
  Housing     = "fs_housing",
  Utility     = "fs_utility",
  Healthcare  = "fs_healthcare",
  'Child Care' = "fs_childcare"
)

# Parent Distress and Child Behavior each have two independent axes:
# which measure, and which threshold (Lower/Higher). Everything below
# is derived from these two lists so a column rename only has to happen
# in one place. "Any" is the composite across every individual measure.
PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES <- list(
  Any        = c(Lower = "distress_any_lower", Higher = "distress_any_higher"),
  Depression = c(Lower = "depress_lower",      Higher = "depress_higher"),
  Anxiety    = c(Lower = "anxiety_lower",       Higher = "anxiety_higher"),
  Stress     = c(Lower = "stress_lower",        Higher = "stress_higher"),
  Loneliness = c(Lower = "lonely_lower",        Higher = "lonely_higher")
)
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES <- list(
  Any   = c(Lower = "child_any_lower", Higher = "child_any_higher"),
  Fussy = c(Lower = "fussy_lower",     Higher = "fussy_higher"),
  Fear  = c(Lower = "fear_lower",      Higher = "fear_higher")
)

# Display text for each domain's thresholds, shown in legends and the
# Threshold dropdown. The internal codes (Lower/Higher/Moderate) never
# change; only this wording does.
PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS <- c(
  Lower  = "At least somewhat frequent",
  Higher = "Very frequent"
)
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS <- c(
  Lower  = "At least sometimes true",
  Higher = "Often or very true"
)
FOOD_INSECURITY_THRESHOLD_LABELS <- c(
  Lower    = "Overall",
  Moderate = "Moderate",
  Higher   = "Severe"
)

# One measure's Lower/Higher pair, relabeled with this domain's own
# display text.
composite_vars_for <- function(measures_list, measure_name, threshold_labels) {
  pair <- measures_list[[measure_name]]
  setNames(
    c(pair[["Lower"]], pair[["Higher"]]),
    unname(threshold_labels[c("Lower", "Higher")])
  )
}
# Every measure except "Any", at one fixed threshold.
measures_at_threshold <- function(measures_list, threshold) {
  individual <- measures_list[setdiff(names(measures_list), "Any")]
  vapply(individual, function(pair) pair[[threshold]], character(1))
}

PARENT_DISTRESS_COMPOSITE   <- composite_vars_for(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Any", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
PARENT_DISTRESS_DEPRESSION  <- composite_vars_for(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Depression", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
PARENT_DISTRESS_ANXIETY     <- composite_vars_for(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Anxiety", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
PARENT_DISTRESS_STRESS      <- composite_vars_for(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Stress", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
PARENT_DISTRESS_LONELINESS  <- composite_vars_for(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Loneliness", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
PARENT_DISTRESS_LOWER       <- measures_at_threshold(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Lower")
PARENT_DISTRESS_HIGHER      <- measures_at_threshold(PARENT_DISTRESS_MEASURES, "Higher")

CHILD_BEHAVIOR_COMPOSITE <- composite_vars_for(CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES, "Any", CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_FUSSY     <- composite_vars_for(CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES, "Fussy", CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_FEAR      <- composite_vars_for(CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES, "Fear", CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS)
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_LOWER     <- measures_at_threshold(CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES, "Lower")
CHILD_BEHAVIOR_HIGHER    <- measures_at_threshold(CHILD_BEHAVIOR_MEASURES, "Higher")

# "Any Non-Parental Care" is left out here on purpose. It's still
# computed as a fallback inside the domain logic, but only these 3
# mutually informative types get reported.
CHILD_CARE_TYPES <- c(
  'Parent-Only Care'       = "parent_only_care",
  'Center-Based Care'      = "center_based_care",
  'Non-Center-Based Care'  = "non_center_based_care"
)

HEALTHCARE_OVERALL       <- c('Missed Well-Baby/Well-Child Check-Up' = "missed_checkup")
FOOD_INSECURITY_OVERALL  <- c('Food Insecure' = "fi_insecure")

# Severity classification. A separate export from FOOD_INSECURITY_OVERALL
# above, not a replacement, same Lower/Moderate/Higher pattern as Parent
# Distress and Child Behavior.

# 2. Sheet name safety (Excel forbids / \ ? * [ ] : in a sheet name, and
#    caps names at 31 characters)


sanitize_sheet_name <- function(name) {
  invalid_chars <- c("/", "\\", "?", "*", "[", "]", ":")
  for (ch in invalid_chars) {
    name <- gsub(ch, "-", name, fixed = TRUE)
  }
  substr(name, 1, 31)
}



# 3. Build the 8-column export table for one month x group x outcome cut


# Excel shows every month, including ones suppressed for low sample
# size or with zero valid responses, with a Reason column explaining
# why. Unlike the dashboard (which blanks a suppressed value so it can
# never leak into a plot), Excel always shows the real computed
# %/Rolling % alongside the Reason text. The workbook is meant to be a
# full record of everything calculated, not a publication-safe view.

# @param monthly_all One row per month, with suppressed/suppress_reason.
# @param rolling_all One row per month (same rows as monthly_all) with
#   its own independent rolling_suppressed/rolling_suppress_reason. A
#   month can be individually suppressed while its rolling estimate
#   still shows, or the other way around, so these never assume the
#   monthly suppressed flag.
build_export_table <- function(monthly_all, rolling_all, month_col = "month") {
  rolling_slim <- rolling_all %>%
    dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(month_col), rolling_n, rolling_weighted_prop,
                  window_months, rolling_suppressed, rolling_suppress_reason)

  monthly_all %>%
    dplyr::arrange(date) %>%
    dplyr::left_join(rolling_slim, by = month_col) %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Month                 = .data[[month_col]],
      N                     = n,
      'Monthly %'           = round(weighted_prop * 100, 1),
      'Rolling N'           = rolling_n,
      '3-Month Rolling %'   = round(rolling_weighted_prop * 100, 1),
      'Rolling Window'      = window_months,
      Reason                = suppress_reason,
      'Rolling Reason'      = rolling_suppress_reason
    )
}



# 4. Sheet writer: one tab, with styled header blocks stacked vertically


HEADER_STYLE <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fontColour = "#FFFFFF", fgFill = "#4472C4", textDecoration = "bold", halign = "center"
)
GROUP_STYLE <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fgFill = "#D9E2F3", textDecoration = "bold"
)
OUTCOME_STYLE <- openxlsx::createStyle(
  fgFill = "#E2EFDA", textDecoration = "bold"
)
EXPORT_TABLE_NCOL <- 8  # Month, N, Monthly %, Rolling N, 3-Month Rolling %, Rolling Window, Reason, Rolling Reason

# If outcome_var_col is given, blocks are nested outcome first, then
# group second (if group_var is also given), then the table. If only
# group_var is given, one block per group level. If neither is given,
# it's a single plain table (the Overall tab for a single-outcome
# domain).

# @param monthly_all,rolling_all Kept as two parallel data frames
#   (rather than one pre-merged table) so group/outcome filtering only
#   has to happen once, consistently, on both.
write_export_sheet <- function(wb, sheet_name, monthly_all, rolling_all,
                                group_var = NULL, outcome_var_col = NULL,
                                month_col = "month") {
  sheet_name <- sanitize_sheet_name(sheet_name)
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
  current_row <- 1
  ncol <- EXPORT_TABLE_NCOL

  write_table_block <- function(monthly_sub, rolling_sub, label = NULL, style = NULL) {
    if (!is.null(label)) {
      openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol, rows = current_row)
      openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, label, startCol = 1, startRow = current_row)
      openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet_name, style, rows = current_row, cols = 1:ncol, gridExpand = TRUE)
      current_row <<- current_row + 1
    }
    table <- build_export_table(monthly_sub, rolling_sub, month_col)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, table, startCol = 1, startRow = current_row,
                         headerStyle = HEADER_STYLE)
    current_row <<- current_row + nrow(table) + 2
  }

  write_group_blocks <- function(monthly_sub, rolling_sub) {
    if (is.null(group_var)) {
      write_table_block(monthly_sub, rolling_sub)
    } else {
      levels_present <- sort(unique(stats::na.omit(monthly_sub[[group_var]])))
      for (lvl in levels_present) {
        write_table_block(
          dplyr::filter(monthly_sub, .data[[group_var]] == lvl),
          dplyr::filter(rolling_sub, .data[[group_var]] == lvl),
          label = lvl, style = GROUP_STYLE
        )
      }
    }
  }

  if (is.null(outcome_var_col)) {
    write_group_blocks(monthly_all, rolling_all)
  } else {
    for (outcome_label in unique(monthly_all[[outcome_var_col]])) {
      openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol, rows = current_row)
      openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, outcome_label, startCol = 1, startRow = current_row)
      openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet_name, OUTCOME_STYLE, rows = current_row, cols = 1:ncol, gridExpand = TRUE)
      current_row <- current_row + 1
      write_group_blocks(
        dplyr::filter(monthly_all, .data[[outcome_var_col]] == outcome_label),
        dplyr::filter(rolling_all, .data[[outcome_var_col]] == outcome_label)
      )
    }
  }

  openxlsx::setColWidths(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol, widths = c(10, 8, 12, 10, 16, 30, 50, 50))
}



# 5. Top-level export functions, one per domain


# Every grouping tab a domain workbook gets: Overall, then each
# demographic grouping, then Source -- same groupings the dashboard's
# Trends tab offers (ALL_GROUPING_LABELS). LA County is handled
# separately below, as its own geography tab, not through this list --
# it's a geography scope now, not a grouping.
GROUPING_TABS <- c(list(Overall = NULL), GROUPING_VARS, list(Source = "Source"))

# Finds every level's already-computed trend for one (domain, figure,
# grouping) cut inside `cuts` (R/06_reporting.R's
# build_all_trend_and_monthly_tables() output) and reshapes it into
# exactly what calc_trend(df, outcome_var, group_var = group_col_name)
# would have returned directly. No calculation happens here, only
# relabeling and stacking rows that are already computed.
# @param group_col_name NULL for Overall (exactly one level, no group
#   column needed); the real column name otherwise.
combine_cut_levels <- function(cuts, domain_key, figure_title, grouping_label, group_col_name) {
  matching <- Filter(function(cut) {
    !is.null(cut) && identical(cut$domain_key, domain_key) &&
      identical(cut$fig$title, figure_title) && identical(cut$grouping_label, grouping_label)
  }, cuts)

  if (length(matching) == 0) {
    stop("No cuts found for domain '", domain_key, "', figure '", figure_title,
         "', grouping '", grouping_label, "'. figure_title has to match a DOMAIN_FIGURES title exactly.")
  }

  if (is.null(group_col_name)) return(matching[[1]]$trend)

  list(
    monthly_all = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(matching, function(cut) {
      dplyr::mutate(cut$trend$monthly_all, "{group_col_name}" := cut$level_name)
    })),
    rolling_all = dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(matching, function(cut) {
      dplyr::mutate(cut$trend$rolling_all, "{group_col_name}" := cut$level_name)
    }))
  )
}

# Keeps only the outcome labels this workbook wants, out of everything
# computed for the figure (e.g. the Material Hardship figure covers
# "Any" plus all 5 types in one cut; the two Material Hardship
# workbooks each keep a different subset of that same cut).
filter_trend_outcomes <- function(trend, outcome_var_col, outcome_labels) {
  if (is.null(outcome_var_col) || is.null(outcome_labels)) return(trend)
  list(
    monthly_all = dplyr::filter(trend$monthly_all, .data[[outcome_var_col]] %in% outcome_labels),
    rolling_all = dplyr::filter(trend$rolling_all, .data[[outcome_var_col]] %in% outcome_labels)
  )
}

# Writes every grouping tab for one (domain, figure) cut into an
# already-open workbook, reusing cuts rather than recomputing anything.
# When outcome_labels narrows the cut down to exactly one outcome (e.g.
# Material Hardship's shared cut, kept to just "Any"), no outcome header
# block is drawn, same as a workbook built from a genuinely
# single-outcome figure -- a single remaining label isn't worth a
# section heading of its own.
#
# One geography's worth of cuts in, one geography's worth of tabs out
# -- Overall, then every demographic grouping, then Source, ALL
# resolved within whichever geography `cuts` came from. This gets
# called once per geography (see export_domain_figure() below), not
# once with a combined CA+LA cuts list: each geography needs its own
# full grouping breakdown (not just a single pinned "LA County" line),
# and several grouping tab names (e.g. "Dual/Non-Dual Parent
# Household") already sit right at Excel's 31-character sheet name
# limit, leaving no room for a "CA - "/"LA - " prefix on the same
# sheet -- hence two separate files instead of one workbook with twice
# the tabs.
#' @param cuts One geography's cuts (build_all_trend_and_monthly_tables_by_geo()'s
#'   `cuts` for CA Statewide, or `cuts_la` for LA County).
.export_figure_across_tabs <- function(wb, cuts, domain_key, figure_title,
                                        outcome_var_col = NULL, outcome_labels = NULL) {
  render_outcome_col <- if (!is.null(outcome_var_col) && (is.null(outcome_labels) || length(outcome_labels) != 1)) {
    outcome_var_col
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  for (tab_label in names(GROUPING_TABS)) {
    group_col <- GROUPING_TABS[[tab_label]]
    trend <- combine_cut_levels(cuts, domain_key, figure_title, tab_label, group_col) %>%
      filter_trend_outcomes(outcome_var_col, outcome_labels)
    write_export_sheet(wb, tab_label, trend$monthly_all, trend$rolling_all,
                        group_var = group_col, outcome_var_col = render_outcome_col)
  }
}

# Export one domain figure (e.g. "Material Hardship by Source", filtered
# to just the "Any" outcome) to one standalone workbook, for ONE
# geography's cuts.
export_domain_figure <- function(cuts, domain_key, figure_title, output_path,
                                  outcome_var_col = NULL, outcome_labels = NULL) {
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  .export_figure_across_tabs(wb, cuts, domain_key, figure_title,
                              outcome_var_col = outcome_var_col, outcome_labels = outcome_labels)
  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, output_path, overwrite = TRUE)
}


# Export every domain to its own workbook in output_dir, from cuts
# R/06_reporting.R already computed for the dashboard. Each workbook
# writes its own file, fully independent of the others, so they run in
# parallel. If one fails, the rest still finish; the failure is
# surfaced clearly afterward instead of silently stopping everything
# partway through.
export_all_domains <- function(cuts, cuts_la, output_dir = EXCEL_OUTPUT_DIR) {
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  path <- function(name) file.path(output_dir, name)

  # Which (domain, figure) this workbook pulls from, and which outcome
  # labels inside that figure's cut it keeps. NULL outcome_labels means
  # keep everything the figure already has.
  jobs_spec <- list(
    "1a_Material_Hardship_Any"     = list(domain_key = "material_hardship", figure_title = "Material Hardship by Source", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = "Any"),
    "1b_Material_Hardship_By_Type" = list(domain_key = "material_hardship", figure_title = "Material Hardship by Source", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = names(MATERIAL_HARDSHIP_TYPES)),
    "2a_Parent_Distress_Composite" = list(domain_key = "parent_distress", figure_title = "Composite: Any Measure (Both Thresholds)", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "2b_Parent_Distress_Lower"     = list(domain_key = "parent_distress", figure_title = paste0("Four Measures — ", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS[["Lower"]]), outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "2c_Parent_Distress_Higher"    = list(domain_key = "parent_distress", figure_title = paste0("Four Measures — ", PARENT_DISTRESS_THRESHOLD_LABELS[["Higher"]]), outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "3a_Child_Behavior_Composite"  = list(domain_key = "child_behavior", figure_title = "Composite: Any Measure (Both Thresholds)", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "3b_Child_Behavior_Lower"      = list(domain_key = "child_behavior", figure_title = paste0("Fear/Fussy — ", CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS[["Lower"]]), outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "3c_Child_Behavior_Higher"     = list(domain_key = "child_behavior", figure_title = paste0("Fear/Fussy — ", CHILD_BEHAVIOR_THRESHOLD_LABELS[["Higher"]]), outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "4_Child_Care_Types"           = list(domain_key = "child_care", figure_title = "Child Care by Type", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL),
    "5_Healthcare"                 = list(domain_key = "healthcare", figure_title = "Missed Well-Baby/Well-Child Check-Ups", outcome_var_col = NULL, outcome_labels = NULL),
    # "Overall" inside this severity breakdown is the exact same number
    # as the old standalone fi_insecure measure (byte-identical case_when
    # logic in R/03_domains.R), so a separate plain workbook would only
    # ever duplicate this one's first block -- one file covers all 3
    # levels.
    "6_Food_Insecurity"            = list(domain_key = "food_insecurity", figure_title = "Severity (3 Thresholds)", outcome_var_col = "outcome", outcome_labels = NULL)
  )

  # Every job_spec runs twice -- once against the CA-wide cuts, once
  # against the LA-county-only cuts -- producing two separate files
  # (e.g. "1a_Material_Hardship_Any_CA.xlsx" and
  # "..._LA.xlsx") rather than one combined workbook. Each file gets
  # the SAME full set of grouping tabs (Overall, Race, Income Level,
  # ..., Source), just resolved within that geography -- not a single
  # "LA County" tab bolted onto the CA workbook.
  geo_variants <- list(CA = cuts, LA = cuts_la)

  tasks <- do.call(c, lapply(names(jobs_spec), function(job_name) {
    stats::setNames(
      lapply(names(geo_variants), function(geo_suffix) list(job_name = job_name, geo_suffix = geo_suffix)),
      paste0(job_name, "_", names(geo_variants))
    )
  }))

  cat("  -- exporting", length(jobs_spec), "workbook(s) x 2 geographies =", length(tasks),
      "file(s) across", PIPELINE_CORES, "core(s)...\n")
  results <- parallel::mclapply(tasks, function(task) {
    t0 <- Sys.time()
    spec <- jobs_spec[[task$job_name]]
    export_domain_figure(geo_variants[[task$geo_suffix]], spec$domain_key, spec$figure_title,
                          path(paste0(task$job_name, "_", task$geo_suffix, ".xlsx")),
                          outcome_var_col = spec$outcome_var_col, outcome_labels = spec$outcome_labels)
    cat(sprintf("     [%s_%s] done, %.1f sec\n", task$job_name, task$geo_suffix,
                as.numeric(difftime(Sys.time(), t0, units = "secs"))))
    NULL
  }, mc.cores = PIPELINE_CORES)
  names(results) <- names(tasks)

  # mclapply() returns a try-error object per failed job rather than
  # halting the other jobs.
  failed <- vapply(results, function(x) inherits(x, "try-error"), logical(1))
  if (any(failed)) {
    stop("export_all_domains() failed on: ", paste(names(tasks)[failed], collapse = ", "),
         "\nFirst error: ", attr(results[failed][[1]], "condition")$message)
  }

  invisible(NULL)
}



# 6. Sample Description export: one workbook, 4 sheets (Overall, By
# Year, By Month, By Survey Number). Each sheet has the same grouping
# breakdown as the dashboard's Sample Description tab, plus an
# FPL_CONT_locf distribution for that same time cut.

# Coarse FPL bins for the histogram block.
FPL_EXPORT_BIN_BREAKS <- c(0, 100, 200, 300, 400, Inf)
FPL_EXPORT_BIN_LABELS <- c("0-100% FPL", "101-200% FPL", "201-300% FPL", "301-400% FPL", "Above 400% FPL")

# pivot_wider() only creates a column for a time value if at least one
# row actually has it. A time period with nobody reporting FPL never
# gets a column at all, so add it back filled with fill_value, so every
# sheet always has one column per time_order entry.
ensure_all_time_columns <- function(wide_df, time_order, fill_value = NA_character_) {
  for (col in setdiff(time_order, names(wide_df))) wide_df[[col]] <- fill_value
  wide_df
}

# EXACT unique-participant counts (distinct CALID, never a response/row
# count) by (grouping, level, time), parameterized on the time column
# so one function builds the Year, Month, and Survey Number cuts. Each
# sheet's time_col partitions df into non-overlapping buckets (a
# response belongs to exactly one year, one month, or one survey
# number), so n_distinct(CALID) per (time_col, grouping) cell is always
# exact here -- no cross-bucket summing/approximation needed, unlike
# the dashboard's own Sample Description tab, which has to support an
# arbitrary custom date range on top of its 3 fixed exact units (see
# R/06_reporting.R's sample_description_breakdown()).
sample_description_counts_by_time <- function(df, time_col) {
  count_distinct <- function(data, ...) {
    data %>%
      dplyr::group_by(...) %>%
      dplyr::summarise(n = dplyr::n_distinct(CALID), .groups = "drop")
  }

  overall <- count_distinct(df, .data[[time_col]]) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grouping = "Overall", level = "Overall")

  by_source <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Source)) %>%
    count_distinct(.data[[time_col]], Source) %>%
    dplyr::rename(level = Source) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(grouping = "Source", level = as.character(level))

  by_grouping <- purrr::map_dfr(names(GROUPING_VARS), function(label) {
    col <- GROUPING_VARS[[label]]
    df %>%
      dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[col]])) %>%
      count_distinct(.data[[time_col]], .data[[col]]) %>%
      dplyr::rename(level = !!col) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(grouping = label, level = as.character(level))
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(overall, by_source, by_grouping) %>%
    dplyr::rename(time = !!time_col) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(time = as.character(time)) %>%
    dplyr::select(grouping, level, time, n)
}

# Pivot the long counts to one row per (Category, Level), one column
# per time value, "N (%)" formatted as a percent of that category's own
# total within that time period, not the grand total.
# @param time_order Column order, left to right, already character and
#   in the order the columns should appear.
pivot_sample_description_wide <- function(counts_long, time_order,
                                           category_order = DEFAULT_SAMPLE_DESCRIPTION_CATEGORY_ORDER) {
  wide <- counts_long %>%
    dplyr::group_by(grouping, time) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      Category = grouping, Level = level, time = factor(time, levels = time_order),
      `N (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), pct)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = `N (%)`)

  present_order <- category_order[category_order %in% unique(wide$Category)]

  # Within each Category, Level follows that grouping's own display
  # order (lowest-to-highest FPL for Income Level, etc.) via the same
  # order_grouping_levels() every other Level column in this pipeline
  # respects -- a plain alphabetical arrange() would put Income Level's
  # bands out of numeric order in this workbook too.
  wide %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Category = factor(Category, levels = present_order)) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(Category) %>%
    dplyr::group_modify(~ {
      .x$Level <- factor(.x$Level, levels = order_grouping_levels(unique(.x$Level), as.character(.y$Category)))
      dplyr::arrange(.x, Level)
    }) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Category = as.character(Category), Level = as.character(Level)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Category, Level, dplyr::all_of(time_order))
}

# FPL_CONT_locf summary statistics (N, Mean, Median, SD, Min, P25, P75,
# Max), one column per time value. N here is deliberately a RESPONSE
# count (dplyr::n(), not n_distinct(CALID)) -- a mean/median/SD of a
# per-response value like FPL_CONT_locf needs every response
# contributing to it, not one per participant, unlike the grouping
# breakdown block above it in the same sheet, which is a participant
# headcount. Labeled "N (responses)" rather than bare "N" so the two
# blocks' different N's are never confused for the same thing.
fpl_summary_stats_by_time <- function(df, time_col, time_order) {
  stats_wide <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(FPL_CONT_locf)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(time = as.character(.data[[time_col]])) %>%
    dplyr::group_by(time) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      `N (responses)` = dplyr::n(),
      Mean   = round(mean(FPL_CONT_locf), 1),
      Median = round(stats::median(FPL_CONT_locf), 1),
      SD     = round(stats::sd(FPL_CONT_locf), 1),
      P25    = round(stats::quantile(FPL_CONT_locf, 0.25), 1),
      P75    = round(stats::quantile(FPL_CONT_locf, 0.75), 1),
      Min    = round(min(FPL_CONT_locf), 1),
      Max    = round(max(FPL_CONT_locf), 1),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-time, names_to = "Statistic", values_to = "value") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(time = factor(time, levels = time_order)) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = value)

  stat_order <- c("N (responses)", "Mean", "Median", "SD", "Min", "P25", "P75", "Max")
  stats_wide %>%
    ensure_all_time_columns(time_order, fill_value = NA_real_) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Statistic = factor(Statistic, levels = stat_order)) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Statistic) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(Statistic = as.character(Statistic)) %>%
    dplyr::select(Statistic, dplyr::all_of(time_order))
}

# FPL_CONT_locf histogram, one row per bin, one column per time value,
# same "N (%)" format as the grouping tables.
fpl_histogram_by_time <- function(df, time_col, time_order) {
  binned <- df %>%
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(FPL_CONT_locf)) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      time = as.character(.data[[time_col]]),
      fpl_bin = cut(FPL_CONT_locf, breaks = FPL_EXPORT_BIN_BREAKS, labels = FPL_EXPORT_BIN_LABELS,
                    include.lowest = TRUE, right = TRUE)
    )

  wide <- binned %>%
    dplyr::count(time, fpl_bin, name = "n") %>%
    dplyr::group_by(time) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
    dplyr::ungroup() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(
      `FPL Bin` = factor(fpl_bin, levels = FPL_EXPORT_BIN_LABELS), time = factor(time, levels = time_order),
      `N (%)` = sprintf("%s (%.1f%%)", format(n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), pct)
    ) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = `N (%)`)

  wide %>%
    ensure_all_time_columns(time_order, fill_value = NA_character_) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(`FPL Bin`) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(`FPL Bin` = as.character(`FPL Bin`)) %>%
    dplyr::select(`FPL Bin`, dplyr::all_of(time_order))
}

# Write one Sample Description sheet: the grouping breakdown block,
# then the FPL summary-stats block, then the FPL histogram block,
# stacked vertically.
write_sample_description_sheet <- function(wb, sheet_name, df, time_col, time_order) {
  openxlsx::addWorksheet(wb, sheet_name)
  current_row <- 1
  ncol <- 1 + length(time_order)

  write_block <- function(label, table) {
    openxlsx::mergeCells(wb, sheet_name, cols = 1:ncol, rows = current_row)
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, label, startCol = 1, startRow = current_row)
    openxlsx::addStyle(wb, sheet_name, OUTCOME_STYLE, rows = current_row, cols = 1:ncol, gridExpand = TRUE)
    current_row <<- current_row + 1
    openxlsx::writeData(wb, sheet_name, table, startCol = 1, startRow = current_row, headerStyle = HEADER_STYLE)
    current_row <<- current_row + nrow(table) + 2
  }

  counts_long <- sample_description_counts_by_time(df, time_col)
  write_block("Respondent Counts by Category", pivot_sample_description_wide(counts_long, time_order))
  write_block("FPL_CONT (% of Poverty Line) -- Summary Statistics (responses, not participants)", fpl_summary_stats_by_time(df, time_col, time_order))
  write_block("FPL_CONT (% of Poverty Line) -- Distribution (% of responses, not participants)", fpl_histogram_by_time(df, time_col, time_order))
}

# Writes all 4 of one geography's sheets (Overall, By Year, By Month,
# By Survey Number), each time cut's own column set recomputed from
# THAT geography's own df -- so e.g. a survey wave that never reached
# LA County doesn't show up as an (empty) column on the LA County
# sheets.
# @param sheet_prefix Prepended to each of the 4 sheet names (e.g.
#   "CA - " / "LA - "); openxlsx sheet names cap at 31 characters, so
#   this has to stay short.
.write_sample_description_sheets_for_geo <- function(wb, master_analysis, sheet_prefix) {
  df <- master_analysis %>% dplyr::mutate(.overall_time = "All Years")

  write_sample_description_sheet(wb, paste0(sheet_prefix, "Overall"), df, ".overall_time", "All Years")
  write_sample_description_sheet(wb, paste0(sheet_prefix, "By Year"), df, "survey_year",
                                  sort(unique(as.character(df$survey_year))))
  write_sample_description_sheet(wb, paste0(sheet_prefix, "By Month"), df, "month",
                                  sort(unique(as.character(df$month))))
  write_sample_description_sheet(wb, paste0(sheet_prefix, "By Survey Number"), df, "SurveyNumber",
                                  as.character(sort(unique(df$SurveyNumber))))
}

# The full Sample Description workbook: Overall (no time split), By
# Year, By Month, By Survey Number -- each duplicated as a CA
# Statewide set of sheets and an LA County (la_county == 1) set, same
# split as the dashboard's Sample Description tab's two geography tabs.
# @param master_analysis master_core after R/01_prep.R (needs Source,
#   every GROUPING_VARS column, survey_year, month, SurveyNumber,
#   la_county, and FPL_CONT_locf).
# @param path Output .xlsx path.
build_sample_description_workbook <- function(master_analysis, path) {
  wb <- openxlsx::createWorkbook()
  .write_sample_description_sheets_for_geo(wb, master_analysis, "CA - ")
  .write_sample_description_sheets_for_geo(wb, dplyr::filter(master_analysis, la_county == 1), "LA - ")

  openxlsx::saveWorkbook(wb, path, overwrite = TRUE)
  invisible(wb)
}
