# dashboard_plots.R # # The dashboard's interactive (plotly) trend-line figure, with hover # tooltips, zoom, a range slider, and built-in PNG/SVG export. # # One plot, for one series (Monthly or Rolling, never both at once). A # single level draws one line with a confidence band and no legend. Multiple # levels draw one line per level in a consistent color, no band, and a # legend above the plot. # # Plots are registered for "plotly_relayout" events (drag, zoom, # double-click reset) under a caller-supplied source id. Paired with # build_window_stats_ui() below and app.R's record_visible_range(), # this lets the dashboard show live averages and response/participant # counts for whatever window is currently in view. See app.R for how # the two are wired together. library(dplyr) library(plotly) library(htmltools) #' The HTML title+caption markup a plot's title uses. Factored out so #' app.R's live window-caption updater can push a fresh title into an #' already-rendered plot with the same markup. plot_title_html <- function(title, caption) { paste0( "", title, "
", "", caption, "" ) } #' Build one interactive figure for one series (Monthly or Rolling). #' #' @param data One row per (level, month): needs level, date, n, and #' either weighted_prop/weighted_ci_low/weighted_ci_high (series = #' "monthly") or rolling_weighted_prop/rolling_weighted_ci_low/ #' rolling_weighted_ci_high/rolling_n (series = "rolling"). #' @param series "monthly" or "rolling". #' @param show_ci Draw the confidence band. Only drawn when data has #' exactly one level, since overlapping bands across several subgroup #' lines would be unreadable. #' @param title Plot title. #' @param caption Small text shown under the title. #' @param source_id Unique id for plotly::event_data("plotly_relayout", #' source = source_id). Give each plot on a page a different id or #' their events overwrite each other. NULL disables event registration. build_interactive_trend_plot <- function(data, series = c("monthly", "rolling"), show_ci = FALSE, title = "", caption = "", source_id = NULL) { series <- match.arg(series) # Even with nothing to plot, a source_id must still get registered # for "plotly_relayout" -- otherwise any later poll of that source # (window_stats_ui()/update_plot_for_window()) warns "event ... is # not registered" on every reactive flush, since event_data()'s # check runs in a deferred onFlushed() callback a suppressWarnings() # around the poll itself can't reach. empty_registered_plot <- function() { if (is.null(source_id)) return(NULL) plotly::plot_ly(source = source_id) %>% plotly::event_register("plotly_relayout") } if (nrow(data) == 0) return(empty_registered_plot()) est_col <- if (series == "monthly") "weighted_prop" else "rolling_weighted_prop" low_col <- if (series == "monthly") "weighted_ci_low" else "rolling_weighted_ci_low" high_col <- if (series == "monthly") "weighted_ci_high" else "rolling_weighted_ci_high" n_col <- if (series == "monthly") "n" else "rolling_n" series_label <- if (series == "monthly") "Monthly" else "Rolling" plot_data <- data %>% dplyr::transmute(level, date, est = .data[[est_col]], low = .data[[low_col]], high = .data[[high_col]], n = .data[[n_col]]) %>% dplyr::filter(!is.na(est)) if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) return(empty_registered_plot()) # Respects the caller's own intended order when `level` arrives as an # ordered factor (e.g. income bands lowest to highest, or Food # Insecurity's Overall/Moderate/Severe) instead of always sorting # alphabetically, which would otherwise scramble either of those. levels_present <- if (is.factor(plot_data$level)) { levels(droplevels(plot_data$level)) } else { sort(unique(plot_data$level)) } single_level <- length(levels_present) == 1 draw_ci <- show_ci && single_level color_map <- if (single_level) { stats::setNames(unname(TREND_SERIES_COLORS[[series_label]]), levels_present) } else { build_level_color_map(levels_present) } p <- if (is.null(source_id)) plotly::plot_ly() else plotly::plot_ly(source = source_id) for (lvl in levels_present) { lvl_data <- plot_data %>% dplyr::filter(level == lvl) %>% dplyr::arrange(date) color <- unname(color_map[lvl]) if (draw_ci) { p <- p %>% plotly::add_ribbons( data = lvl_data, x = ~date, ymin = ~low * 100, ymax = ~high * 100, line = list(width = 0), fillcolor = color, opacity = 0.15, showlegend = FALSE, hoverinfo = "skip", name = paste(lvl, "95% CI") ) } # Built as a plain vector here, not a plotly formula, because a # formula referencing `lvl` would evaluate lazily and every trace # would end up showing the loop's final value instead of its own. hover_text <- sprintf("%s
%s: %.1f%%
n = %d", lvl, format(lvl_data$date, "%B %Y"), lvl_data$est * 100, lvl_data$n) # A dropped/suppressed month just isn't a row here at all (plot_data # already filtered those out above) -- connectgaps defaults to # FALSE, but with no gap rows to break on, the line simply skips # straight from one real point to the next instead of showing a # visible break. p <- p %>% plotly::add_trace( data = lvl_data, x = ~date, y = ~est * 100, type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", name = lvl, showlegend = !single_level, line = list(color = color, width = 2), marker = list(color = color, size = 6), text = hover_text, hoverinfo = "text" ) } p <- p %>% plotly::layout( title = list( text = plot_title_html(title, caption), font = list(size = 14), x = 0, xanchor = "left", y = 0.98, yanchor = "top", pad = list(t = 8, b = 8) ), xaxis = list(title = "", rangeslider = list(visible = TRUE, thickness = 0.08), type = "date"), yaxis = list(title = "Percentage (%)", rangemode = "tozero"), # Horizontal legend above the plot, not to the right, so the plot # keeps its full width. Plotly wraps it onto more rows on its own # when there are too many levels for one line. # # legend.y uses plotly's default frame (relative to the data area, # where 1.0 is its top edge), not yref = "container" -- the # bundled plotly.js doesn't support legend.yref, so that silently # falls back to sitting inside the plot. A y above 1 reliably # pushes the legend into the margin instead. legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, xanchor = "left", y = 1.2, yanchor = "top", font = list(size = 11)), hovermode = "closest", # Top margin sized for the common case: title + caption, plus a # legend that usually wraps to 1-2 rows. margin = list(t = if (single_level) 95 else 130, b = 40, r = 40, l = 55), autosize = TRUE ) %>% plotly::config(displaylogo = FALSE, modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("lasso2d", "select2d")) if (!is.null(source_id)) p <- p %>% plotly::event_register("plotly_relayout") p } #' Round a date down to the 1st of its own calendar month. floor_to_month_start <- function(d) as.Date(format(d, "%Y-%m-01")) #' Round a date up to the last day of its own calendar month. ceiling_to_month_end <- function(d) seq(floor_to_month_start(d), by = "1 month", length.out = 2)[2] - 1 #' Snap a c(min_date, max_date) to whole calendar months. A mouse drag #' operates at day-level resolution, but every row's date sits on the 1st #' of its month, so without snapping a drag landing mid-month would #' silently exclude that month from any downstream calculation. snap_to_full_months <- function(date_range) { c(floor_to_month_start(date_range[1]), ceiling_to_month_end(date_range[2])) } #' Extract the raw, unsnapped c(min_date, max_date) a "plotly_relayout" #' event payload represents. Returns NULL if the payload can't be parsed #' or represents an autorange reset. parse_relayout_range <- function(relayout_event) { if (is.null(relayout_event)) return(NULL) if (isTRUE(relayout_event[["xaxis.autorange"]])) return(NULL) lo <- relayout_event[["xaxis.range[0]"]] hi <- relayout_event[["xaxis.range[1]"]] if (is.null(lo) || is.null(hi)) { rng <- relayout_event[["xaxis.range"]] if (is.null(rng) || length(rng) < 2) return(NULL) lo <- rng[[1]]; hi <- rng[[2]] } parsed <- suppressWarnings(as.Date(substr(as.character(c(lo, hi)), 1, 10))) if (anyNA(parsed) || parsed[1] > parsed[2]) return(NULL) parsed } #' Render compute_window_stats()'s output as a small HTML stats panel: #' one row per level, with the currently visible window's averages, #' responses, and participants, so these update as the user drags the #' plot's range slider. #' @param stats compute_window_stats()'s output. #' @param date_range The window it was computed over. build_window_stats_ui <- function(stats, date_range) { if (is.null(stats) || nrow(stats) == 0) { return(htmltools::tags$div(class = "text-muted", style = "font-size:12px;", "No months with data in the selected window.")) } window_label <- sprintf("%s – %s", format(date_range[1], "%b %Y"), format(date_range[2], "%b %Y")) n_months <- stats$n_months[1] # Every row shares the same window, so this is one value in practice, # but read defensively (all()) in case that ever stops being true. is_exact <- isTRUE(all(stats$is_exact_participants)) cell_style <- "border: 1px solid #ddd; padding: 4px 10px;" header_cell_style <- paste(cell_style, "background-color: #f5f5f5; text-align:left; color:#555; font-weight:600;") rows <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(stats)), function(i) { s <- stats[i, ] htmltools::tags$tr( htmltools::tags$td(s$level, style = paste(cell_style, "font-weight:600;")), htmltools::tags$td(sprintf("%.1f%%", s$n_weighted_avg * 100), style = cell_style), htmltools::tags$td(sprintf("%.1f%%", s$unweighted_avg * 100), style = cell_style), htmltools::tags$td(format(s$total_responses, big.mark = ","), style = cell_style), htmltools::tags$td(format(s$total_participants, big.mark = ","), style = cell_style) ) }) # Only worth a loud warning when it's actually approximate -- an exact # count gets a quiet, affirmative note instead of competing for # attention with the one case that actually matters to flag. participants_note <- if (is_exact) { htmltools::tags$div( style = "font-size:12px; color:#2E7D32; margin-top:2px; max-width:320px; white-space:normal;", "Participants is an exact count for this full range." ) } else { htmltools::tags$div( style = "font-size:12px; color:#a33; margin-top:2px; max-width:320px; white-space:normal; font-weight:600;", "Participants is approximate here: it sums each month's own distinct-respondent count, which can double-count anyone who answered in more than one month of this custom window." ) } htmltools::tags$div( style = "font-size:12px; max-width:100%; overflow-x:auto;", htmltools::tags$div( style = "color:#666; margin-bottom:4px;", sprintf("Window: %s (%d month%s)", window_label, n_months, if (n_months == 1) "" else "s") ), htmltools::tags$table( style = "border-collapse: collapse; border: 1px solid #ddd; max-width:100%;", htmltools::tags$thead(htmltools::tags$tr( htmltools::tags$th("", style = header_cell_style), htmltools::tags$th("N-wtd avg", style = header_cell_style), htmltools::tags$th("Unwtd avg", style = header_cell_style), htmltools::tags$th("Responses", style = header_cell_style), htmltools::tags$th("Participants", style = header_cell_style) )), htmltools::tags$tbody(rows) ), participants_note ) } #' The Investigate tab's deviation-bar plot: a shared reference line with #' one bar per selected demographic level, showing how far that level's #' rate differs from the shared reference average. Bars are colored by #' grouping, not by level or direction, so every level of one grouping #' reads as one color family. A level with no reliable data in the #' investigation period draws as a zero-length bar at the reference line, #' labeled "Suppressed". #' #' @param comparison compute_multi_level_comparison()'s output. Call this #' only when comparison$valid is TRUE. build_multi_level_comparison_plot <- function(comparison, title = "", caption = "") { lvl <- comparison$levels ref <- comparison$reference if (is.null(lvl) || nrow(lvl) == 0) return(NULL) # "Overall" first, since match() returns NA for it otherwise (it isn't # one of GROUPING_VARS/"LA County"), and order() sorts NA last, burying # the bar most directly comparable to the reference line. Within a # grouping, order by that grouping's own semantic order (e.g. Income # Level low-to-high) instead of plain alphabetical, which would bury # e.g. "$100,000 or more" before "$25,000-$49,999". grouping_order <- c("Overall", names(GROUPING_VARS), "LA County") lvl$level_rank <- NA_integer_ for (g in unique(lvl$grouping)) { idx <- lvl$grouping == g ordered_levels <- order_grouping_levels(unique(lvl$level[idx]), g) lvl$level_rank[idx] <- match(lvl$level[idx], ordered_levels) } lvl <- lvl[order(match(lvl$grouping, grouping_order), lvl$level_rank), ] lvl$axis_label <- sprintf("%s (n=%s)", lvl$level, format(lvl$n, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)) # rev() so plotly's bottom-up categorical axis still reads top-to-bottom. lvl$label <- factor(lvl$axis_label, levels = rev(lvl$axis_label)) ref_pct <- ref$chosen_avg * 100 axis_title <- if (identical(ref$avg_type, "unweighted")) "Unweighted %" else "Weighted %" lvl$pct <- lvl$weighted_prop * 100 lvl$color <- unname(GROUPING_COLORS[lvl$grouping]) lvl$color[is.na(lvl$color)] <- "#898781" lvl$bar_label <- ifelse( lvl$suppressed, "Suppressed", sprintf("%.1f%% (%+.1f pts)", lvl$pct, lvl$deviation_pts) ) lvl$bar_base <- ref_pct lvl$bar_value <- ifelse(lvl$suppressed, ref_pct, lvl$pct) lvl$bar_delta <- lvl$bar_value - lvl$bar_base # The reference line stays the horizontal center of the plot. The # x-axis range is symmetric around it and adjusts to the data. max_dev <- max(abs(c(lvl$bar_value, ref_pct) - ref_pct), na.rm = TRUE) if (!is.finite(max_dev) || max_dev == 0) max_dev <- 5 pad <- max_dev * 1.35 x_range <- c(ref_pct -
